motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing item 14.A. to be placed on the Scheduled Items for further discussion. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item pulled out
motions.summary: The council approved its bundle of routine consent items but pulled the Mountainland Supply development agreement out for separate discussion.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the batch of routine business the council passes in a single vote, minus the one item it wanted to debate on its own.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Development Agreement with Mountainland Supply
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Development Agreement with Mountainland Supply. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Development deal with Mountainland Supply approved
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Mountainland Supply; the motion itself does not state the site, the size, or the terms.
motions.impact: A development agreement locks in what a builder may do on a specific piece of land. The motion doesn't say where that land is or what is going up, so the details sit in the agreement itself.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 and using the price of the land at $45,000 per acre ($1.03 per square foot) nothing the parcel does not require additional water rights
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 and using the price of the land at $45,000 per acre ($1.03 per square foot) nothing the parcel does not require additional water rights. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: failed for lack of a majority vote, 1:4.
motions.headline: Lower $45,000-an-acre price rejected
motions.summary: The council rejected a lower price of $45,000 per acre ($1.03 per square foot) for the same city land, on the argument that the parcel needs no added water rights.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this was a competing price for the same parcel, and the higher price the council approved is what stands.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 and directed Staff to work on refining water requirements and draft a policy to ensure consistent review of future Land Disposal Applications
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 and directed Staff to work on refining water requirements and draft a policy to ensure consistent review of future Land Disposal Applications. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: failed for lack of a majority vote, 2:3.
motions.headline: Bid to pause the land sale over water rules fails
motions.summary: The council declined to delay the land-sale resolution while staff refined water requirements and wrote a policy for reviewing future requests to buy city land.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this was an attempt to hold the sale back for more study, and it did not hold.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 with a sales price of $95,000 per acre ($2.18 per square foot)
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 with a sales price of $95,000 per acre ($2.18 per square foot). Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City land to be sold at $95,000 an acre
motions.summary: The council authorized selling a significant piece of city-owned property at a price of $95,000 per acre, or $2.18 per square foot.
motions.impact: The motion doesn't name the parcel or the buyer; what it settles is the price the city will accept for land the public currently owns. Nothing changes day to day for residents.

motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to add drafting a Telecommunications Ordinance and/or Franchise Agreement to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Telecom rules added to council's priority list
motions.summary: The council added drafting a telecommunications ordinance and/or franchise agreement to its list of legislative priorities.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for you yet — this puts the item on the city's to-do list, and any actual rules would have to come back to the council later.

motions.item_title: Add drafting a policy for code adoption to guide Staff in evaluating Land Disposal Applications…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add drafting a policy for code adoption to guide Staff in evaluating Land Disposal Applications to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Land-sale policy added to council's priority list
motions.summary: The council put writing a policy for how staff review applications to buy city-owned land onto its list of legislative priorities.
motions.impact: Nothing changes right now — this only commits the city to drafting rules later for how it handles requests to buy public land.
